briefs.source_chain: Fed hikes 25bp unanimously with hawkish dots (16/18 seeing another hike this year, higher longer-run median) that sit awkwardly against Warsh's 'non-restrictive'/'dose of accommodation' framing, therefore alongside upgraded growth and inflation forecasts JPM reads a shift from supply-shock to demand-led overheating risk, therefore JPM keeps its call for one more hike in December.
briefs.brief_chain: Same: unanimous 25bp hike, hawkish dots (16/18, 14/18 for 2027) in tension with Warsh's framing, upgraded growth/unemployment/inflation forecasts read as demand-led overheating risk, JPM keeps its December hike call.

distortions.what: Brief paraphrases Warsh's 'hard-pressed to describe policy as restrictive' as 'calling policy non-restrictive'
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — same substantive claim (Warsh denies restrictiveness), just inverted phrasing; JPM's December-hike call is unaffected.

briefs.source_chain: Fed hikes 25bp unanimously with a hawkish dot plot, therefore markets reprice more tightening (75bp by June, ~50% October odds) and yields/dollar rise while equities fall (cushioned by an oil pullback on Saudi/Libya supply news), therefore DB raises its own call to 50bp more via December and March hikes; separately UK CPI cools BoE hike odds and US data (strong retail sales, weak NAHB) round out the day.
briefs.brief_chain: Same: unanimous 25bp hike and hawkish dots drive repricing and a yield/dollar rise with equities down but cushioned by the oil pullback, DB ups its call to 50bp more (Dec+March), UK CPI cuts BoE hike odds, US retail sales/NAHB noted.

distortions.what: Brief omits Trump's post-decision rate comment and Warsh's 'dose of accommodation'/moderate-tightening-cycle framing
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — neither detail bears on DB's own 50bp forecast or the market-pricing read; pure compression.

briefs.source_chain: Oil supply disruptions (Yanbu suspension, Libya outages, no Hormuz reopening) revive stagflation fears and push oil and yields to multi-year highs, hurting equities and Bitcoin, therefore going into the Fed decision markets price a 94% hike probability built from Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole remarks plus a strong jobs report and hot core CPI, therefore DB's economists expect the hike with the live question being how the dot plot signals further guidance.
briefs.brief_chain: Same: oil-driven stagflation fears push oil/yields to multi-year highs and hit equities/Bitcoin, Fed hike odds build from ~30% in July through Jackson Hole to 94% today reinforced by jobs/CPI data, DB expects the hike and frames the dot-plot guidance question.

distortions.what: Brief generalizes the source's precise 'within 3% / less than 4% of highs' figures for S&P/STOXX to 'within single digits of their highs'
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — rounding/generalization preserves the same magnitude and point (indices still near highs despite the selloff).

briefs.source_chain: A hike is almost fully priced so the Fed must deliver, therefore ING weighs 25bp (the market discount, criticized by Warsh's own guidance-to-pricing-to-delivery loop) against a control-asserting 50bp that could calm or instead destabilize the long end, landing on 25bp as its call and ruling out no-change as unlikely; separately, term-premium forces (JGB yields, thin euro swap liquidity, US deficits) keep the long end bear-steepening and sticky even if oil eases, leaving ING more pessimistic on the 2027 US outlook.
briefs.brief_chain: Same: ING calls 25bp over a 50bp option that could either calm or destabilize the long end, rules out no-change as unlikely, and separately expects term-premium-driven bear steepening to persist while turning more pessimistic on 2027 US growth.

distortions.what: Brief omits the source's boom/bust and AI-cycle-vs-peak-growth framing for why term premium could keep rising
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — this is exploratory color around the term-premium call, not part of ING's actual positioning (25bp hike call, bear-steepening view, 2027 pessimism), all of which the brief retains.
